messages.text: 19th to victory! Antonelli sensationally wins thrilling Italian GP

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli completed a remarkable comeback to win his home Italian Grand Prix from 19th place after a race-long battle against Mercedes team-mate George Russell.
metadata.content: Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli sensationally wins thrilling Monza race from George Russell and Max Verstappen | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Italian GP: Kimi Antonelli sensationally wins thrilling Monza race from George Russell and Max Verstappen Championship leader Kimi Antonelli became the first Italian to win at Monza since 1966 after an incredible drive from 19th to first; Antonelli had stunning pace to come through the field, then later caught George Russell in the closing laps; Max Verstappen claimed his fifth podium of 2026 Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 6 September 2026 16:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc had a huge crash on the opening lap of the Italian GP Kimi Antonelli completed a remarkable comeback to win his home Italian Grand Prix from 19th place after a race-long battle against Mercedes team-mate George Russell. Antonelli was not expected to contend for victory due to grid penalties for exceeding his engine allocation but stormed through the field early on - in between the red flag for Charles Leclerc's huge crash - and showed tremendous pace to catch Russell on an alternative strategy. The two Mercedes and Max Verstappen pulled clear of the field in the first half of the race, exchanging the lead several times, due to the yoyo style of racing caused by the 2026 power units and the impact of having a slipstream around the long straights at Monza. metadata.summary: Katie Taylor acclaimed becoming a three-time undisputed world champion in her farewell fight at Croke Park as the most special moment of her decorated career.
metadata.content: Katie Taylor ecstatic after beating Flora Pili to make perfect end to ‘dream career’ at Dublin's Croke Park | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Katie Taylor ecstatic after beating Flora Pili to make perfect end to ‘dream career’ at Dublin's Croke Park Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972. Sunday 6 September 2026 12:36, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the fight between Katie Taylor and Flora Pili Katie Taylor acclaimed becoming a three-time undisputed world champion in her farewell fight at Croke Park as the most special moment of her decorated career. Taylor outclassed Flora Pili in a unanimous points victory in front of a crowd of 80,000 to ensure her three decades as an amateur and professional boxer ended in fairytale fashion. Wild celebrations followed the announcement that she had overwhelmed the previously unbeaten Pili 100-90 100-90 98-91 on the scorecards. For Taylor the feeling of signing off in front of her fans bettered winning Olympic gold at London 2012, headlining Madison Square Garden and her trilogy against Amanda Serrano. Francis-Henri Graffard's star returns having not being seen since his third in the Prince Of Wales's Stakes - where there were excuses for the run given his misbehaviour in the stables prior to the race. That run is the only blemish to an otherwise seamless four-year-old campaign to date, which has seen him win the Prix Ganay & Prix Aga Khan IV, showing a devastating turn of foot in both.
